content:
Hi! just want to share my two current goals for complexity theory in CSLib.
The first is to refactor the MultiTapeTM API to work with RunPath, which represents a finite path through a Turing machine’s configuration graph. There are two nice things about this:

  1. It provides a unified concept for deterministic and nondeterministic Turing machines, so many lemmas about RunPath apply to both models. In fact, MultiTapeTM already extends MultiTapeNTM.
  2. Homomorphisms between configuration graphs let us map run paths between related Turing machines and reuse proofs. A good example is Cslib/Computability/Machines/Turing/MultiTape/Plumbing/ExtendTapes.lean, where this approach makes the definitions and proofs more concise.

My second goal is to merge the formalization of the classical result SPACE(o(log log n)) = SPACE(1). This is my second attempt formalizing this result, and the new API makes the proof much shorter.

Here is the PR stack for these goals:

CSLib PR My fork PR Description Git diff (+/− lines)
#1145 #37 Moves the shared space lemmas for run paths to Space.lean, next to the space definitions. +90 / −122, 7 files
#1122 #31 Removes the duplicate deterministic space measures and uses the shared space API on computation paths. +179 / −241, 4 files
#1151 #32 Generalizes extendTapes, outputToTape, and inputFromTape to nondeterministic machines through a common adapter. +156 / −147, 5 files
#1152 #12 Uses visit sequences to shorten sufficiently long inputs while preserving a chosen storage of a halting deterministic computation. +582 / −26, 6 files
#1153 #39 Introduces the ComputesSuchThat hierarchy to share the definitions of computation with time, space, and combined bounds. +103 / −8, 1 file
#1154 #13 Proves SPACE(o(log log n)) = SPACE(1) using input shortening, with corresponding computability and decidability results. +215 / −0, 5 files
